label: mid-sequence k/m/h/1/x/t input after an early b/g/j/s/f
explanation: Almost only active in the original (input) phase (99% of mass), at positions 3-7, and never at t=0-1. Within that window it fires when the input is one of a set of consonants/digits, ranked k > m > h > 1 > x > t, then weaker for 2, y, d. It is boosted when the sequence starts with b, g, j, s or f (first_tok lift 2-4x; prev2_tok b 4.5x). It is mostly the first occurrence of the token in the sequence (93% of mass). The strongest activations are k at t=4-5 after prefixes like s g j b or j b u b. It is nearly silent on the delimiter and during copying, and on q, v, e and the other letters. The response looks graded, the sum of an input-token term and an accumulated-context term, so a boolean rule does only moderately well: on dev, P=0.42, R=0.52, F1=0.46, mass recall 0.63. A looser version (any b/g/j/s/f seen earlier, plus 2/y/d added to the token set) gets mass recall 0.81 but precision 0.23. Many steps with the right token and context still stay below threshold, which suggests other prefix tokens suppress it.
